blocks.text: Great work on the vowels! Now let's add your first consonant sound: K. The five kana in this row are just K plus each vowel you already know: ka, ki, ku, ke, ko. Say them out loud as you go — it really helps them stick.

blocks.hint: Looks like a person kicking a ball — KA-pow!
Like a KEY with two teeth on the left.
Like a KEG lying on its side with a tap.
Two short lines — a COrd coiled up.

blocks.text: Chant the whole row in a rhythm: KA KI KU KE KO. Every consonant row follows this same a-i-u-e-o order, so this pattern will serve you again and again.
か き く け こ あ か き え こ
blocks.title: Read this aloud

questions.prompt: Which kana is read "ka"?
questions.explanation: か is ka — the one that looks like a person kicking.

questions.prompt: How do you read か?
questions.explanation: か is K plus a = ka.

questions.prompt: Which kana is read "ki"?
questions.explanation: き is ki — think of a KEY.

questions.prompt: How do you read き?
questions.explanation: き is K plus i = ki.

questions.prompt: Which kana is read "ku"?
questions.explanation: く is ku — the bird's beak shape.

questions.prompt: How do you read く?
questions.explanation: く is K plus u = ku.

questions.prompt: Which kana is read "ke"?
questions.explanation: け is ke — think of a KEG.

questions.prompt: How do you read け?
questions.explanation: け is K plus e = ke.

questions.prompt: Which kana is read "ko"?
questions.explanation: こ is ko — two short coiled lines.

questions.prompt: How do you read the word こ え?
questions.explanation: こ is ko and え is e, so こ え is ko e — it means voice.

notes: Spaces go between words, never between the kana of one word: write こえ (koe), not こ え (ko e), in examples, readings, prompts and choices. Choose example words an adult traveller would use, such as えき (station), over rare ones such as かき (persimmon).

original_draft.title: Reading real words with every sound

blocks.text: ともだち と がっこう。 おかあさん の しゃしん。 ちょっと みて。
blocks.title: Read this

blocks.text: Nice work! These are real words with every tricky sound you have learned: long vowels like おかあさん and がっこう, the small っ in ちょっと and がっこう, and the small ゃ in しゃしん. Read each word slowly and let your eyes catch every kana.
Watch the small っ. In がっこう you pause slightly before こ. In ちょっと you pause before と. That tiny gap is real — say it!
Watch the long vowels. おかあさん has a long お-あ sound, and がっこう ends in a long こ-う sound. Stretch them out.
The small ゃ joins with し in しゃしん, so し + ゃ = しゃ, one quick sound. Don't say two separate sounds.

templates.hint: Read ともだち out loud, then type what you hear.
Remember the small っ pause and the long こう sound.
Stretch the long お-あ at the start.
し + ゃ is one quick sound: しゃ.
Small ょ joins ち, then a small っ pause before と.

questions.prompt: In the passage, which word means "friend"?
questions.explanation: ともだち means friend. It is the very first word in the passage.

questions.prompt: Read the word and type exactly how it sounds in kana: ともだち
questions.explanation: ともだち — four plain kana, no tricky sounds here.

questions.prompt: Which word in the passage means "school"?
questions.explanation: がっこう means school. Note the small っ pause and the long こう sound.

questions.prompt: Read the word and type exactly how it sounds in kana: がっこう
questions.explanation: がっこう — small っ for the pause, and こう is a long vowel.

questions.prompt: Whose photograph is in the passage?
questions.explanation: The passage says おかあさん の しゃしん — mother's photograph.

questions.prompt: Read the word and type exactly how it sounds in kana: おかあさん
questions.explanation: おかあさん — the お-あ at the start is a long vowel, so write both kana.

questions.prompt: Which word in the passage means "photograph"?
questions.explanation: しゃしん means photograph. The し + ゃ makes one quick しゃ sound.

questions.prompt: Read the word and type exactly how it sounds in kana: しゃしん
questions.explanation: しゃしん — remember the small ゃ joins し to make しゃ.

questions.prompt: Which word in the passage means "a little"?
questions.explanation: ちょっと means a little. It has a small ょ and a small っ pause.

questions.prompt: Read the word and type exactly how it sounds in kana: ちょっと
questions.explanation: ちょっと — ち + small ょ, then a small っ pause before と.

notes: When GRAMMAR TAUGHT SO FAR is (none), the passage may use only words the learner knows: no particles such as と, の, を, に, が or か, and no verb forms such as みて. Write it as labels or a short list (for example captions on photos), and make every comprehension question answerable from known words alone. Describe a long vowel by the kana that is held: in おかあさん the あ makes か last two beats (it is not お-あ), and in がっこう the う makes こ last two beats. Word typed checks as "Read this word and type how it sounds: <word>", never "type it in kana", because learners type rōmaji.

blocks.text: Time to make your first real sentences! In Japanese, you can say 'A is B' with a simple pattern: A は B です. Think of it as 'A, as for it, is B.'
The word です (desu) goes at the end. It's like 'is' or 'am' or 'are.' It makes your sentence polite and finished. Super useful — you'll use it constantly.

blocks.japanese: わたし は いしゃ です 。

blocks.text: See that は? Here's the tricky part: when は is used this way (as a topic marker), you read it as 'wa', NOT 'ha'. The spelling stays は, but the sound is 'wa'. It marks the topic — the thing you're talking about.
は points at your topic like a little sign saying 'as for THIS...'. And remember: topic は is pronounced 'wa'.

blocks.japanese: あなた は せんせい です 。
ともだち は がくせい です 。

blocks.text: To ask a question, just add か at the end: あなた は いしゃ です か 。 means 'Are you a doctor?' Easy, right?

blocks.label: Listen to A は B です sentences

templates.hint: Find the topic marker — remember it's read 'wa' here
Put は right after the topic (the thing you're talking about)
です means 'is/am/are' and sits at the end
Finish the sentence with です

questions.prompt: Which word means 'is / am / are' and ends a sentence?
questions.explanation: です goes at the end and means 'is/am/are'. It makes the sentence polite.

questions.prompt: Finish the sentence: わたし は がくせい ___ 。 (I am a student.)
questions.explanation: A は B です — the sentence ends with です.

questions.prompt: In あなた は せんせい です 。 how is は pronounced?
questions.explanation: When は is a topic marker, you read it 'wa', even though it's spelled は.

questions.prompt: Type this sentence in kana: 'My friend is a doctor.' (friend = ともだち, doctor = いしゃ)
questions.correctAnswer: ともだち は いしゃ です
questions.explanation: Topic ともだち, then は, then いしゃ, then です. Great work!

notes: Teach only this lesson's grammar. Do not preview the next grammar point (the A は B です draft taught か, which is the next lesson's target). Wrong choices must also be taught words or grammar, so no untaught particles such as か or を as distractors. Include at least one check that asks what a whole sentence means. In a typed sentence check, say "rōmaji is fine" so the learner knows no Japanese keyboard is needed. Put 。 straight after the last word, with no space before it.

blocks.text: Have you noticed the tiny っ inside some words? It is a small version of つ, and it is special. It has no sound of its own. Instead, it is a short silent beat — a little pause — right before the next sound.
Here is the one rule: when you see a small っ, stop for one beat, then hit the next sound a bit harder. Think of it like holding your breath for a split second before the next letter pops out.
Let's read your new words out loud. Pause where the っ sits, then say the next sound strongly: がっこう (school) — say 'ga', pause, then 'kkou'.
Small っ = a speed bump. You slow down, pause, then go again. If you forget the pause, がっこう turns into 'gakou' and sounds wrong!

blocks.label: Listen to the small っ pause

templates.hint: You go here to learn. Pause at っ: ga-(pause)-kkou.
You need this to ride a train. ki-(pause)-ppu.
Something you read with pictures and articles. za-(pause)-sshi.

questions.prompt: Which word means 'school'?
questions.explanation: がっこう is 'school'. Pause at the っ: ga-(pause)-kkou.

questions.prompt: Read this word and type how it sounds: がっこう
questions.explanation: Nice! がっこう — remember the little pause at っ.

questions.prompt: Which word means '(doing) together'?
questions.explanation: いっしょ means 'together'. Say i-(pause)-ssho.

questions.prompt: Read this word and type how it sounds: いっしょ
questions.explanation: Great! いっしょ with a short pause at っ.

questions.prompt: Which word means 'a little'?
questions.explanation: ちょっと means 'a little'. Pause: cho-(pause)-tto.

questions.prompt: Read this word and type how it sounds: ちょっと
questions.explanation: Perfect! ちょっと — don't forget the pause at っ.

questions.prompt: Which word means 'ticket'?
questions.explanation: きっぷ means 'ticket'. Say ki-(pause)-ppu.

questions.prompt: Read this word and type how it sounds: きっぷ
questions.explanation: Yes! きっぷ with the little pause at っ.

questions.prompt: Which word means 'magazine'?
questions.explanation: ざっし means 'magazine'. Pause: za-(pause)-sshi.

questions.prompt: Read this word and type how it sounds: ざっし
questions.explanation: Well done! ざっし — a short pause at っ.

notes: In a sound lesson with typed reading checks: describe timing in beats, as the long-vowel lesson does, and give how a word sounds in kana (say が, stay silent for one beat on っ, then say こう), not in rōmaji. Rōmaji stays in the kana cards, with one exception: when a sound has no rōmaji of its own, such as the small っ, give one worked example that says how it is typed (In rōmaji, a small っ doubles the next letter, so you type がっこう as gakkou) and leave the other words for the learner to work out. The explanation of a typed reading check may be shown after a wrong answer, so do not open it with praise: give the rōmaji answer (In rōmaji, きっぷ is kippu: the っ doubles the p). Do not write a word's rōmaji in any other explanation or hint, because a typed check asks the learner to read that word. Do not ask "Have you noticed" about a sound the learner has not met yet.
